adventure.title: The Glass Saint
adventure.synopsis: A museum reliquary bursts on the eve of Saint Olyra’s procession. Before sunset, independent witnesses must recover its stolen petition-bed, expose the lie beneath the city’s obedient saint, and decide whether grief may borrow a body and command through every bell.
adventure.premise: At noon on the eve of Saint Olyra’s procession, the rehearsal bell bursts the museum reliquary from within. The painted devotional copy remains; the engraved silver bed beneath it has been cut away. Curator Iria Vale invokes the emergency witness charter, opening the sealed gallery, restricted archive, procession court, and abandoned bell chapel to independent inspection. Her authority ends at Vale Manor, where her family keeps Olyra’s true heartglass, and her interest prevents her from certifying the case against them. The council will not halt the sunset procession without proof of immediate danger. Witnesses, records, petitioners, bellkeepers, and the divided Vales can establish what Tavia Sorn stole, what Olyra died doing, and what Edrin Vale has built to make the city hear. A warrant, a public case, a broken peal, a bargain, or forced entry may reach the winter garden. None decides who should hold the relic or what the recovered truth requires.
adventure.explanation:
Sixty-three years ago, museum founder and former council archivist Alis Vale replaced Saint Olyra’s heartglass with a painted devotional copy. During the Ash Fever, Olyra defied the council, opened the sealed west infirmary, and died among the patients she refused to abandon. The civic cult kept her authority by reversing her act: Olyra became the saint of obedience. Alis hid her deposition and the names of the patrons who ordered the doors sealed, but kept the authentic heartglass at Vale Manor. The trustees found the substitution during recent conservation and chose silence again.

Alis’s grandson Edrin has spent years authenticating the record. When the trustees offered one more closed review after the procession, he chose the hour when the city would already be listening. Assistant conservator Tavia Sorn joined him because the withheld material included her family’s petitions and an ancestor’s infirmary record. She set a bell-metal answer-pin beneath the case. The rehearsal note made it ring, threw the glass outward, and hid her removal of the silver vow-bed. Tavia carried the bed through the procession court, passed it to Edrin, and fled with a cut archive leaf toward the House of Petitions. She expects the rite to give the buried record a voice. She does not know that it takes one.

The rite joins four materials: Olyra’s heartglass, the petition-engraved vow-bed, knot geometry rehearsed in the Bell Chapel, and panes from Olyra’s first shrine. Six decades of pleas, thanks, slogans, and demands give the silver its language. The heartglass contributes a residue of Olyra, never a recoverable person. The procession peal gives the result reach. The first long note raises a body from reflected petitions. The second takes the natural voice of the nearest living Vale inside the winter garden’s outer pane circle. The third sends one command through every fitted procession bell until dawn. Edrin begins on the speaker mark and intends to pay the vocal cost. Iria is endangered only if she enters the circle or remains there after Edrin is moved beyond it. The mouth stage fails without either a Vale inside or a hand closing the inner line.

Six answer-pins cast from the old infirmary bell connect the apparatus. The museum trigger is cracked and spent. Three pins in the Grand Belfry carry the witness, mouth, and crown notes. Relay pins at East Gate and River Ward repeat the crown command but cannot raise the body or take a speaker. The chapel holds a working counterkey: a notched tuning strip that identifies and lifts live pins, a braided reversal cord that changes the outer knot, and a pitch table keyed to Olyra’s deposition. Each part enables different work. At the belfry, investigators can prevent a stage, confine the crown note, sound a warning, or preserve the peal; every cut rope, lifted pin, and altered knot remains altered.

The investigation contests who may make a fact public. Provost Helian Dorr and the trustees fear riot, scandal, and institutional ruin. They will preserve the procession until confronted with evidence they cannot fold back into a private review. The House of Petitions claims the vow-bed as public property and can provide witnesses, custodians, or current petitions. Bellmaster Jori Kest can delay, mute, or retune the peal when given technical proof and either lawful or public protection. Edrin will pause for a hearing that already possesses records, witnesses, and a custody plan. He will not surrender to another sealed promise. The finale may preserve or destroy the heartglass, dismantle the speaking body, permit a bounded answering rite, or allow the full awakening. Whatever speaks is a composite of relic, record, petition, and civic expectation: a disputed civic voice assembled by the living.

Advance pressure through acts the table can see. Dorr issues containment after a report, accusation, or request reaches him. The answer-pins wake after Edrin has assembled the manor apparatus and Dorr has authorized the final bell test. The procession moves when its hold expires or fails. The first note needs the grand-tower crew; the second needs Edrin to close the inner knot around a Vale; the third needs the crown bell and an intact launch pin. Change any of those facts and the sequence changes. Edrin and Dorr learn through runners, watch reports, public bells, and witnesses. Neither answers information that never reaches him.

Carry five public facts from scene to scene: how widely the rupture’s cause is known; where authenticated copies are held; what authority Captain Renn possesses; whether the procession follows its published course; and which witnesses have committed to speak. These facts persist. A public copy cannot be recalled, a signed witness keeps the commitment, and a written denial becomes evidence of its own. Gains may conflict: publicity can protect records and frighten families; a warrant can secure objects and concentrate them under one seal. Carry those mixed results into the belfry and manor.

Keep four pages distinct during route-open play. **Access** names the doors, routes, and scheduled spaces that can be reached. **Knowledge** names supported claims. **Authority** names what a charter, seal, warrant, custodian, or witness permits. **Ritual state** names the pins, knots, materials, notes, and relays still in play. Knowledge of a place grants no entry; a warrant proves no history; a maintenance passage supplies no counterkey; a stopped bell settles no custody. When separated investigators reunite, record what each saw, changed, received permission for, or still only infers.

Unvisited places continue through fixed hands and channels. Tavia goes from the court to the House unless intercepted. Dorr acts on reports that reach him. Senna logs and protects the archive; publication requires someone present to choose and carry a packet. Petition caucuses carry their own copies and demands. The chapel counterkey stays where Edrin left it until someone removes it. The belfry crew follows the latest order and evidence placed before them. Record each off-screen movement. Late arrival changes custody, access, and pressure; the location and its people retain what has already happened.

Before the winter-garden doors open, carry forward the facts already made. Record the surviving stage and relay pins, any warning peal, the holders of the records, Renn’s authority, the witnesses in motion, and the positions of Iria and Tavia. Six ways into the winter garden remain: a warranted carriage gate, Iria’s family claim, Tavia’s service route, the infirmary-frame maintenance passage, a public advance behind the warning crowd, or direct force. Each brings different witnesses, hazards, and claims to custody.

The winter garden binds five things the rite cannot lose: the shrine-pane crown, the vow-bed, the heartglass cradle, the inner mouth knot, and the bell trunk under the floor. The mouth note takes the nearest living Vale inside the outer pane circle when the note completes. Edrin begins nearest. Iria becomes the target only by entering or remaining inside after he leaves. The ordinary transfer fails without a Vale inside the circle or a hand closing the inner line. The complete counterkey can instead bind a willing breath-giver into a limited answering form. That speaker risks muteness until dawn rather than involuntary permanent loss.

First decide what the bells did to a body and voice. Then decide what the city does with it. Record whether the body formed, whose voice was taken, the command and its range, the surviving condition and custodian of every object, the witnesses to each stage, and all injuries or detentions. Then record publication, prosecution, surviving compulsion, and Olyra’s changed public memory. Edrin’s surrender and silent bells leave the public argument intact. The city may recover the truth of Olyra’s defiance and still disagree about ownership, punishment, sainthood, and what defiance demands now.

references.title: Saint Olyra
references.summary: An Ash Fever healer whose defiance was recast as obedience; her surviving heartglass carries relic residue, never a recoverable person or final civic judgment.
references.content:
## Historical record

Olyra served during the Ash Fever. When the council ordered the west infirmary sealed and refused reinforcement, she opened its doors from within, organized water and burial work among the patients, and died there. Her unsigned deposition, patient indexes, family copies, marked cloth, bed-frame names, and the two fever doors preserve different parts of that act.

## Civic image and surviving material

The later civic cult reversed her defiance into obedience. Alis Vale removed Olyra’s authentic heartglass from the museum reliquary, installed a painted devotional copy, and moved panes from the first infirmary shrine to Vale Manor. The procession, sermons, petitions, relic, and suppressed papers therefore carry competing public Olyras.

## Authority and limits

Olyra is dead and cannot consent to custody, choose a current cause, command the city, or certify what later institutions say in her name. The heartglass contributes residue to Edrin’s working, while the vow-bed, copied records, living petitions, borrowed voice, reflected crowd, and bells contribute the rest. Any Glass Saint is a disputed composite assembled by the living. Survivor families retain authority over their own testimony, relics, grief, and present commitments.

references.title: Iria Vale
references.summary: The museum curator who opens the independent inquiry and presses for disclosure; her Vale position, prior closed review, museum seal, and possible place inside the mouth circle limit what she may certify, surrender, or safely risk.
references.content:
## Charter and office

Iria Vale is the museum curator. She works through accession, disclosure, witness charters, counter-signed copies, and written custody entries. At the shattered reliquary she invokes the emergency witness charter before Provost Dorr can close the room. The charter reaches museum rooms, consensual staff interviews, independent inspection, and a written entry whenever evidence moves.

## Vale accountability

Iria wants the concealed history published, but she belongs to the family that kept Olyra’s heartglass and benefited from the false display. She must make her prior obedience to closed review, family knowledge, custody choices, and use of the museum seal visible as the inquiry advances. A public acknowledgment can unlock household cooperation and sharpen the case against continued concealment; it cannot surrender another Vale’s property or excuse Edrin’s coercive plan.

## Voice risk and limits

The mouth note takes the nearest living Vale inside the winter garden’s outer pane circle. Edrin begins nearest. Iria becomes vulnerable only through her actual position after entry, never merely through kinship or curatorial office. Her charter grants no manor search, compelled testimony, ownership, warrant, or certification against her family. She may speak for herself and her office; independent custody and authentication must come from other hands.

references.title: Edrin Vale
references.summary: The principal antagonist: a meticulous Vale historian who exposes a true civic concealment by building a rite that can steal one living voice and compel the city through its bells.
references.content:
## Grievance and manner

Edrin Vale is Alis Vale’s grandson. He spent years authenticating Olyra’s suppressed history and documenting the trustees’ renewed silence. He prefers exact argument, exhibits his evidence, accepts personal cost, and refuses another private promise after the procession. His grievance is sound; his chosen remedy remains coercive.

## The undertaking

Edrin receives the stolen petition-bed from Tavia, joins it to Olyra’s heartglass and old shrine panes at Vale Manor, and connects the apparatus to answer-pins and the sunset peal. He begins on the speaker mark intending to lose his own voice. He knows the first note forms a reflected body, the second takes the nearest living Vale voice inside the circle, and the third can carry one command through fitted bells until dawn.

## Authority, posture, and limits

Edrin controls his participation, household access available to him, the apparatus he assembled, and whether he opens or closes its knots. He has no authority to take another voice, compel listeners, assign public custody, or make a composite manifestation settle Olyra’s meaning. He pauses for a hearing that already has public anchors, records, witnesses, and credible custody. Two independent anchors plus named custody can move him toward witnessed terms. Private seizure, destroyed copies, or unannounced assault harden him, though he takes no hostages and attacks no surrendered witness.

references.title: Tavia Sorn
references.summary: An assistant conservator and culpable accomplice who steals the vow-bed to force publication, then may turn against the rite when she learns that its second note takes a living voice.
references.content:
## Work and culpability

Tavia Sorn is an assistant conservator whose family petitions and infirmary record were among the material withheld by the museum and trustees. She helped plan the rupture, set the museum answer-pin, removed the silver vow-bed under cover of the burst case, passed it to Edrin in the procession court, and carried a cut archive leaf toward the House of Petitions. Lio’s injury, sabotage, theft, and evidence removal remain hers.

## What she wants

Tavia wants the buried record outside closed Vale and trustee custody before sunset. She joined Edrin expecting a reflected witness, not an involuntary speaker. Proof of the vocal cost can divide her from him because she never accepted that price. She expects arrest after cooperation and does not treat confession as absolution.

## States, authority, and limits

In defiance, Tavia admits the theft to Nessa, refuses private trustee custody, and withholds the manor service route while testing whether investigators mean to bury the pages. Proof of voice loss plus credible outside custody moves her toward cooperation: she gives the transfer statement, chapel deliveries, service route, and public rejection of the mouth stage. Captain Renn’s public seal can carry her testimony into lawful custody. A closed transfer ordered by Dorr ends cooperation; threatened private seizure or summary violence sends her toward the infirmary. Tavia may confess, testify, distribute her copy, and reveal routes she used. She cannot speak for the Sorn families, authorize Edrin’s rite, or place current petitions into it for absent petitioners.

references.title: Provost Helian Dorr
references.summary: The senior trustee and procession marshal who protects civic order, institutional custody, and the full peal by turning dangerous evidence back toward sealed process.
references.content:
## Office and manner

Helian Dorr is provost, senior museum trustee, and procession marshal. He speaks through schedules, holds, routes, seals, crowd order, and paper that can be entered as the city’s official account. He is not Edrin’s occult partner. His obstruction is procedural, reputational, and material.

## What he wants

Dorr wants the procession preserved, the rupture contained as vandalism and theft, and credible evidence returned to a review he can stage-manage. He fears panic, scandal, loss of institutional custody, and the consequences of admitting that trustees repeated the original concealment. He can accept a short delay, bounded inspection, or divided custody when immediate danger becomes harder to suppress than the record.

## Authority and limits

Dorr controls the trustee agenda, museum containment orders, procession seal, and official peal direction. He may suspend public archive access, request seizure, order holds within civic authority, and place written refusals into the record. He cannot unmake witnessed copies, invent Tavia’s location, erase independent testimony, command private Vale property without process, or make unsupported dismissal survive public authentication. Reports, runners, bells, signed statements, and witnesses define what he knows. His orders remain evidence, including narrow orders, refusals, and obstruction.

references.title: Captain Ors Renn
references.summary: The watch captain who can preserve evidence, protect people, detain named suspects, and execute narrow written authority without deciding publication or relic ownership.
references.content:
## Office and practice

Captain Ors Renn commands the watch response around the rupture, procession, and manor. He works through named suspects, exact written scope, public seals, custody logs, evacuation, and bounded force. He is an enforcement authority, not an investigator who converts every supported claim into permission.

## Available authority

At the museum Renn can seal the gallery, preserve evidence, and detain a named suspect. With a property-recovery, emergency-entry, or safety-inspection order, he can bring officers through the named route, protect servants and ringers, seal listed objects, and restrain people identified within the order. His public seal can protect Tavia’s testimony and give technical intervention lawful cover.

## Limits

Renn cannot certify Olyra’s history, decide which archive packet investigators should copy, choose publication, transfer ownership, surrender every object to Dorr, or extend a narrow order by convenience. Every action remains bounded by the authority actually written or by an immediate danger he can name. At Vale Manor his exact order determines entry, detention, seizure, evacuation, and the overreach Dorr may later allege.

references.title: Registrar Senna Drail
references.summary: The archive registrar who authenticates exact records, logs every order, and protects originals without choosing absent investigators’ packet or recipient for them.
references.content:
## Keys, seals, and copies

Senna Drail is registrar of the restricted archive. She controls its keys, shelf marks, custody log, and certification seal. She can identify the substitution ledger, Olyra’s deposition, the modern concealment minute, and the contact records that join Edrin to the bell work. Exact copies carry weight because Senna can show what drawer, seal, gap, recipient, and witness belong to each one.

## What she requires

Senna certifies for a lawful recipient or for investigators prepared to defend her office in public. A watch seal, named public custodian, counter-signed reading, or council entry can meet that need. When a request would expose originals or leave a copy easy to bury, she names the missing recipient, protection, or custody step instead of supplying an off-screen rescue.

## Boundaries

Senna preserves and authenticates records. She does not select the investigators’ priority packet, make private evidence public without a carrier, surrender originals to a crowd, or turn the archive into a faction. If Dorr closes the stair, her log preserves the order and the copies already released; late arrivals inherit that changed access state.

references.title: Sister Caldra Fen
references.summary: The healer who runs the surviving west infirmary, protects patients and survivor families, and offers testimony only with ward coverage and custody beyond trustees and Vales.
references.content:
## The working ward

Caldra Fen runs the hospice in the surviving west wing. She controls patient access, the fever doors, and the conditions under which staff or families leave the ward to testify. Care continues during the investigation; the city’s need for proof never converts patients, frames, cloth, or family memory into unattended evidence.

## Testimony and refuge

Caldra can authenticate Olyra’s work through living testimony, the doors, household copies, and material kept outside Vale and museum custody. She will speak when another healer covers the ward and the record has a protected holder. She may shelter Tavia long enough to join confession, the cut leaf, and family testimony, but she will answer a lawful public charge.

## Limits

Caldra speaks for her ward and her own conditions, not for every survivor family. She will not promise a breath-giver, hand patients into a procession, warehouse recovered relics, or let Olyra’s image command the people whose memory authenticates her defiance.

references.title: Nessa Quill
references.summary: The keeper of the House of Petitions who keeps incompatible caucuses copying, names public custodians, and turns authenticated pages into a hearing without pretending the House wants one outcome.
references.content:
## Keeper of moving sheets

Nessa Quill keeps the House of Petitions. She coordinates copyists, family packets, public readings, rear-window distribution, and named keepers while four caucuses argue over what the record should require. Her work preserves words before institutions engrave, burn, seal, or place them beneath a relic.

## Public custody

Nessa can join an authenticated source to a House copy, distribute a packet among several holders, record a public-custody pledge, or assemble witnesses for the belfry and manor. She needs named custodians and a plan that survives seizure pressure; otherwise each caucus carries its own piece toward court, infirmary, manor, or private storage.

## Caucus limits

Nessa cannot make Open Hands, Returned Names, West Door Circle, and Quiet Keepers desire the same ending. She can keep sheets moving, separate a public record from Edrin’s coercion, and protect Tavia’s statement under open custody. She cannot turn copied petitions into consent for the rite or guarantee that a crowd remains orderly.

references.title: Bellmaster Jori Kest
references.summary: The bellmaster who commands the Grand Belfry crew and can strip, lift, warn, or retune only when technical proof and lawful or public protection reach the tower.
references.content:
## Crew authority

Jori Kest directs the Grand Belfry. He assigns hands to ropes, stops or resumes work, reads the warning chart, and protects ringers from unexplained machinery. Dorr’s sealed peal order shields the crew until a warrant, signed hold, named public witnesses, or immediate technical danger gives Kest a defensible reason to alter it.

## What he can verify

The chapel strip can identify the linked pins; the pitch table and Mela Fen’s ledger can match stages to bells; Tavia’s statement can establish deliberate sabotage. With one technical proof and lawful or public protection, Kest can organize controlled work: strip all stage pins, lift the crown pin, sound a warning, or retune the third note.

## Limits

Kest controls the belfry and crew, not the heartglass, petition record, Vale household, or final custody. He acts on evidence that reaches him. A sounded note remains part of the ritual history, and every cut rope, lifted pin, tied branch, frightened junior, and altered order carries forward.

references.title: Alis Vale
references.summary: The dead museum founder who replaced Olyra’s heartglass with a devotional copy, hid the deposition, moved the shrine panes home, and left the warning that bell work could make a Vale voice common property.
references.content:
## The first concealment

Alis Vale founded the museum after serving as a council archivist. She removed Olyra’s authentic heartglass from the public reliquary, installed the painted devotional copy, hid Olyra’s deposition and the patrons behind the fever-door order, and retained the relic at Vale Manor. She later moved the first shrine’s colored panes from the infirmary into the winter garden.

## Records left behind

Alis’s donor letters, transfer receipt, private ledger, and marginal warning join the museum substitution to the manor apparatus. She called the heartglass a family witness and warned that, when rung through the city, the shrine glass could make a family voice common property. Those records authenticate both the concealment and the danger without turning Alis into a living witness.

## Legacy

Alis’s acts gave later Vales custody, leverage, and liability. Her papers can move Tavia, divide trustees, and expose the vocal cost. They cannot supply current consent, settle ownership, or tell Iria and Edrin what family accountability requires now.

references.title: The House of Petitions
references.summary: An independent copy office whose four caucuses preserve petitions, distribute disputed records, and provide public custody without sharing one desired command or finale.
references.content:
## Four tables, one ledger

The House preserves words before they are engraved, burned, sealed, or laid beneath civic relics. Open Hands seek cures, pardons, and debt relief. Returned Names seek missing people and may favor an answering saint. West Door Circle carries infirmary memory and rejects compulsory command. Quiet Keepers fear that street action will close the office.

## What survives the window

Its ledgers show what the petition-engraved silver accumulated over six decades. Copyists can authenticate transfer timing, spread the deposition and concealment minute, name custodians, assemble witnesses, and create a public hearing that Edrin can hear before the bells. If seizure splits the room, each caucus carries a surviving packet to a known destination.

## No petition speaks for the whole city

The House can preserve and weight public language; it cannot author a reliable command, consent for living speakers, or a single civic judgment. Current petitions enter the apparatus only when someone carries and places them. The House may hold copies or recovered silver under a named pledge, while changing caucus positions remain on the public-pressure ledger.

references.title: The West Infirmary
references.summary: The surviving hospice where Olyra opened the fever doors; its patients, frames, cloth, copies, and families preserve evidence outside the museum and Vale household.
references.content:
## The two fever doors

During the Ash Fever, Olyra broke the council seal from within, opened the west doors, organized water and burial work, and died among the patients. Survivors built the first shrine here. Alis Vale later removed its colored panes to the Vale winter garden, leaving empty frames and a service relationship that can still reveal a maintenance route.

## The ward still working

The west wing remains a working ward under Sister Caldra Fen. Bed-frame names, burial cloth, the nailed order, axe cuts, household copies, and living testimony authenticate what the public relic omits. Ilye Aven keeps the tallies; Tomar Ordel holds family instructions; separate households set their own terms for appearing, signing, or keeping evidence.

## Care before testimony

The infirmary can authenticate Olyra’s defiance, shelter records, trace the shrine panes, and place West Door witnesses into a public hearing. It remains a care site. Patients and frames stay where care requires them, no family becomes a ready-made chorus, and late bell effects must be resolved as hazards to the ward rather than convenient support.

references.title: The Vale Winter Garden
references.summary: The manor chamber where shrine panes, petition silver, heartglass, mouth knot, and bell trunk meet; routes and custody may change, but its five joined stations define the finale’s physical logic.
references.content:
## Five things under glass

The winter garden sits inside Vale Manor above an undercroft and bell trunk. Eight old shrine panes form a hinged crown around the petition-engraved vow-bed and suspended heartglass. The inner mouth knot marks the speaker circle. Foundation anchors, shutters, pane latches, floor branches, and the silver-pantry passage make the apparatus physically divisible rather than a single ritual switch.

## Six doors to one circle

Investigators may reach it through a warranted carriage gate, Iria’s family claim, Tavia’s service route, the infirmary-frame maintenance passage, a public advance behind a warning peal, or direct force. Each route brings different witnesses, hazards, access claims, and custody pressure. Knowledge of a route grants no automatic authority over the house or relics.

## What the room fixes

The nearest living Vale inside the outer pane circle faces the mouth note; Edrin begins nearest. Removing panes, lowering heartglass, separating silver, opening knots, or tying branches changes later stages. The operating sheet records the live positions, damage, pins, custody, and public anchors. This record preserves the chamber’s stable layout and entry logic.

references.title: The Grand Belfry
references.summary: The three-level crown tower that carries witness, mouth, and command notes; its crew, machinery, and crown link govern reach while the operating sheet owns each live rope and pin state.
references.content:
## Rope room, wheel loft, crown deck

The ringing room holds ropes, brakes, the peal order, and warning chart. The wheel loft holds moving wheels, counterweights, and three live stage pins. The crown deck holds bell mouths, the tuning ledger, and sight lines to the court and relay towers. Rope lanes, loose weights, and humming metal make position and crew control part of every intervention.

## Three notes and two echoes

The west tenor’s witness pin carries the body note. The silver bell’s mouth pin carries the voice note. The crown pin launches the command. East Gate and River Ward can repeat a crown note that reaches them, but they cannot begin body or mouth stages. Lifting the crown pin protects the city even when earlier stages remain possible.

## What bronze remembers

Jori Kest directs the crew, while Dorr’s sealed order supplies their initial protection. Technical proof plus lawful or public cover can support controlled removal, warning, or retuning. The ritual-and-bell sheet records every sounded note, altered rope, lifted pin, tied branch, relay, injury, and frightened ringer; this record preserves the tower’s stable structure and role.

encounters.title: The Shattered Gallery
encounters.summary: The broken case yields three evidence chains while museum, watch, and trustee authority compete to seal them first.
encounters.opening_view: One last sliver drops from the saint’s case and rings against the floor. Lio Marr bleeds beside the plinth while Ossa Pell chalks the curved spray. The painted figure still hangs in place; beneath it, a clean silver-bed rectangle remains. Provost Dorr calls for the procession doors. Iria Vale spreads the witness charter across his seal before anyone can close the room.
encounters.content:
The rehearsal leaves docent Lio Marr bleeding, a crowd against the doors, and three offices reaching for the wreckage. Iria Vale lays down the emergency witness charter. It permits independent inspection of museum rooms, consensual staff interviews, counter-signed copies, and a written entry whenever evidence moves. It grants no search of private Vale property, compelled testimony, or ownership. Captain Ors Renn can seal the gallery and detain a named suspect. Floor warden Ossa Pell controls keys and handling. Provost Helian Dorr, procession marshal and senior trustee, wants a vandalism report and open doors before sunset. Registrar Senna Drail has taken the archive keys below. Tavia Sorn is absent from roll call.

The painted bone copy remains strapped to cracked plaster. The clean rectangle beneath it held the engraved silver vow-bed. A hidden answer-pin caught the rehearsal note and threw the case glass outward. One mounting screw was loosened in advance; the second was cut during the panic. Packing felt bears Vale carriage wax. Tavia’s numbered narrow saw is gone. Lio saw a grey museum cloak pass through the service door while the room watched the glass. Ossa can trace every key, though she saw no hand lift the silver.

Sort the scene into three evidence chains. The answer-pin and bell dust establish mechanism. The saw, cut mounts, and cloak route establish removal. The felt, wax, and accession number establish provenance and destination. Leave a chain under watch seals, bag it through Ossa with counter-signatures, or take a sample and exact rubbing while the original stays. Watch custody best supports a warrant. Senna’s certification best supports authenticity. Distributed rubbings and statements survive suppression but invite Dorr to call them incomplete. If he gains the originals, preserve what has already left the room: Lio’s statement, investigators’ notes, and every signed copy. The next problem becomes access, not forgotten discovery.

Several jobs can proceed at once. Treat Lio and gain a calm witness. Reconstruct the service-door sight line before boots destroy it. Give Renn a usable description of the stolen silver. Keep Dorr from reopening the gallery before Ossa closes the log. A poor search still finds the outward spray and exact absence. A lost argument produces Dorr’s written order and the objects he chose to seal. Rough handling contaminates one chain, not the whole case. The evidence points toward the court witnesses, the accession record, the chapel’s pin work, the west infirmary named on the backing, and the Vale carriage route. A rush to the manor remains possible; it arrives with less law and fewer witnesses.

**If skipped or left early.** Ossa numbers the evidence, Renn seals the room, and Dorr places unclaimed originals under trustee seal. Lio receives treatment and remains available. The outward rupture, silver-shaped absence, and staff roll stay observable. Tavia reaches the Procession Court, and every copy or note already made continues to circulate. Later entry may require Senna, Renn, or a written challenge to Dorr. The gallery never resets.

The devotional copy’s backing points to the surviving hospice, where doors, frames, and family memory preserve the history absent from the case.
Vale wax and the carriage route point toward the manor chamber where the stolen silver and retained heartglass can be joined.

encounters.title: The Procession Court
encounters.summary: A collapsing civic rehearsal turns Tavia’s transfer into partial public testimony and forces an early choice between pursuit, protection, and publication.
encounters.opening_view: “Stop opening empty carts,” Sergeant Vela Rusk shouts. The petition wagon has sagged under a weight it no longer carries, and a grey museum cloak is trapped beneath its wheel. Lantern children are already being formed into ranks. A copyist runs with a loose page; a trustee’s deputy follows. At the far gate, the Vale carriage turns once in the sun and disappears into traffic.
encounters.content:
The procession’s fixed order makes every break visible. Six watch outriders clear the route. Twenty-four children carry glass lanterns under schoolmistress Anet Vey. Four museum porters bear the silver canopy. A petition wagon and three House copyists follow. West Door families carry white ribbons for the Ash Fever dead; Dorr and the civic officers close the line. The devotional image used outdoors is separate from the shattered case, so Dorr can truthfully say the ceremony can proceed. Sergeant Vela Rusk’s detail is searching carts without knowing what the stolen silver looks like.

Tavia crossed the court in a grey museum cloak with the vow-bed under the petition wagon. Lantern bearer Pellen Vey saw the slats bow. Driver Hara Bex felt the weight and later found fresh Vale wax on a replacement strap. Copyists Iven Quill and Sera Mott saw Edrin’s carriage pause and heard Tavia say, “The city gets the words before you get the bell.” When Officer Den Rusk stopped the wagon, she abandoned the cloak, passed the wrapped silver into the carriage, kept a packet of copied records, and fled toward the House of Petitions. Each witness owns one piece. Assemble the handoff; no statement supplies it whole.

Choose what the court preserves. Pursuit may catch or shadow Tavia before the House. Counter-signed statements give Renn the Vale destination and protect witnesses from later claims of crowd invention. A precise description of the vow-bed releases innocent carts and turns panic into a theft search. Crowd control keeps children, wheels, and glass lanterns from becoming injuries. Public accusation makes suppression harder. The West Door families may remain in the line, withdraw, or carry their ribbons with the evidence; the ceremony changes around that choice.

Public pressure follows acts. Name the silver and carriage before witnesses, and rumor becomes an allegation with owners. Put authenticated pages into the crowd, and Dorr loses the comfort of “vandalism.” Win petitioner or West Door commitments, and the accusation acquires a body. Each gain has a cost: Dorr may advance the procession, trustees may order seizure, and frightened families may leave. Quiet protection can preserve a witness who matters more at the manor than a shouted claim does here.

Tavia’s route fails forward. Intercepted, she admits cutting the bed free, refuses trustee return, and asks for a public custodian; she knows nothing of the vocal cost. Shadowed, she reveals the House’s entrances and allies. Lost, she distributes the cut archive leaf and becomes harder to detain privately. Violence lets her escape, but Pellen, Hara, and at least one copyist remain. Meanwhile the procession continues to take position. Delay changes people, orders, and routes rather than subtracting invisible minutes.

**If skipped or reached late.** Tavia reaches the House with the cut leaf. Edrin’s carriage continues to the manor. The procession advances. Pellen stays with the lantern children, Hara returns to the wagon yard, Iven and Sera go to the House, and Den reports to Renn. Their partial accounts remain available. A late investigation follows people and changed ranks, not a preserved chase.

reference_links.context: The fixed procession order carries the city’s obedient saint into public view while witnesses begin contesting that inherited account.
Her charter reaches the public court, but it supplies access rather than control over witnesses, procession order, or private Vale property.
Receives the stolen vow-bed and continues by carriage to Vale Manor while witnesses and Tavia divide from his route.
Carries the vow-bed through the court, transfers it to Edrin, and leaves witnesses whose statements can name the route.
His procession authority shapes holds, ranks, and official response while public witnesses carry facts beyond his chosen account.
Receives witness reports through the watch and can preserve named testimony without freezing the moving court into a chase scene.
Her copy office is Tavia’s intended destination; court witnesses and the dropped token can carry the transfer account into public custody.
Copyists, tokens, and Tavia’s flight connect the public court to the independent office that can distribute the record before sunset.
The marshal’s cue sheet identifies the crown tower as the source of the three long notes and the lesser towers as followers.

encounters.title: The Archive Vault
encounters.summary: Four record packets prove substitution, suppressed history, modern concealment, and ritual contact—but custody determines what each proof can do.
encounters.opening_view: Three books lie open to the same accession. Heartglass. Substitute. Missing leaf. Registrar Senna Drail checks the pale torn edge of the newest gap, then covers an unsigned deposition with one hand. The vault door stands open only as far as its chain permits. Beside her keys, the custody log waits for its first name.
encounters.content:
Senna has chained the vault door with junior copyists Eren Sol and Mave Kitt inside. Before she opens another drawer, she makes the visitors name a recipient and write the first custody entry. She will certify exact copies that leave through a lawful hand or through investigators willing to defend her office; originals stay under her keys. Dorr may close the public stair. The conservation stair still reaches the vault, but using it costs Senna’s signature and may cost her position.

Four packets compete for the copyists’ hands. The **relic packet** joins accession numbers, conservation photographs, donor letters, and a private receipt proving Alis substituted the painted copy and kept the heartglass at Vale Manor. The **Olyra packet** joins her unsigned deposition, council wax, patient indexes, and sermons that turn refusal into obedience. The **modern suppression packet** contains the six-week-old conservation finding and the trustee minute calling it “credible and materially significant” while postponing publication. The **ritual-contact packet** holds Tavia’s slips, Edrin’s consultation requests, Alis’s warning that a Vale voice may become common property, and the chapel-to-garden bell diagram.

Each packet opens different action. Relic records plus the gallery trail support recovery of the vow-bed. Modern suppression plus an independent witness exposes Dorr’s present obstruction. Olyra’s papers plus the infirmary’s material record authenticate the history. Ritual contact plus an answer-pin supports emergency inspection at the belfry or manor. One certified packet can leave quickly. Two require divided labor and two custodians. A complete set before sunset demands an open vault, outside copyists, or rough copies Dorr can challenge.

Custody gives evidence its reach. A watch seal carries immediate legal force but may lock the packet inside a trustee dispute. Senna’s seal carries museum authentication and endangers her office. The House makes copies public and vulnerable to charges of partisanship. The infirmary lends independent history; Caldra will not turn a working hospice into the city’s warehouse. Distributed copies survive seizure only if signatures preserve their chain. Often the strongest case places different packets in different hands.

If Dorr takes the vault, he seals drawers, removes Senna from duty, and sends one copy to the Trustees’ Chamber. That act creates delay and a named obstruction. It leaves family copies, accession gaps, Tavia’s cut leaf, and every certified packet untouched. Stolen papers retain information but acquire a custody objection. When Senna refuses a dangerous request, she names the evidence or recipient that would let her sign. Reward a chosen packet and a defended custodian; the vault cannot yield everything before sunset.

**If skipped or reached late.** Senna protects the originals and logs every order. She chooses no packet for absent investigators. A suspension closes the public stair and enters Dorr’s signature in the book; the conservation stair, a lawful recipient, or divided trustees can reopen access. Tavia’s cut leaf proves one suppressed passage, never the full relic, Olyra, suppression, or ritual chain. Delay narrows authentication without deleting the archive.

reference_links.context: Her deposition, patient indexes, sermons, and suppressed records form the documentary chain for Olyra’s defiance and later civic revision.
Museum access and counter-signed copying remain useful only through Senna’s independent custody log and recipient rules.
His requests, Alis’s warning, the bell diagram, and the suppressed history establish both his evidence and the voice hazard.
The torn leaf, consultation slips, and custody chain distinguish one suppressed passage from the complete documentary case.
May suspend the public stair and seek sealed custody, but Senna’s log and witnessed copies preserve his orders and the evidence.
Controls originals, certification, custody logs, and the recipients through whom a copied packet can leave the restricted archive.
The infirmary’s material evidence and her conditional testimony supply an independent chain that the archive cannot manufacture by itself.
Her transfer receipt, donor letters, substitution, and vocal warning join the false display to the heartglass and shrine panes kept at the manor.
Survivor indexes and household copies direct authenticators to evidence and witnesses beyond museum and Vale custody.
The bell-and-window diagram, private transfer ledger, and shrine-pane history identify the manor chamber as the apparatus site.

encounters.title: The Trustees’ Chamber
encounters.summary: A divided hearing converts distinct kinds of proof into warrants, delay, public record, or a signed refusal that can travel farther.
encounters.opening_view: Each burst of applause from the court shortens the trustees’ silence. Iria Vale’s empty chair faces the museum seal. Beside Provost Dorr, a clerk has begun two incompatible orders: hold the crown bell for a quarter hour; seize the House of Petitions’ ledgers. Witnesses are called in the order Dorr chooses. The ink remains wet enough for either order to become the city’s answer.
encounters.content:
Four trustees have different breaking points. Helian Dorr controls the agenda and procession seal; he trades minutes for order and resists publication he cannot stage-manage. Collections keeper Irena Moss accepts split custody and a manor recovery warrant when the relic is endangered, but keeps originals away from crowds. Halwen Gorse speaks for guilds and merchants; danger to spectators buys a short delay. Maelin Tress speaks for the west wards and breaks with Dorr once Olyra’s deposition has independent authentication. Iria’s empty chair asks whether she will sit as curator, speak as a Vale, or surrender the museum seal. Captain Renn attends only to request an order.

Build the hearing from four kinds of proof. **Theft** needs the missing vow-bed plus a credible Vale transfer or Tavia’s admission. **Imminent danger** needs chapel notes, a live pin, or a demonstration that the peal can carry compulsion. **Independent authentication** comes from Senna’s chain, infirmary material, or authenticated House copies under a named custodian. **Public witness** requires two counter-signed court statements, a committed petitioner, or someone ready to speak in the chamber. Quality and custody matter. Four versions of one museum claim still count once.

Proof becomes authority in combinations. Theft plus a Vale destination yields a narrow recovery warrant. Danger plus authentication yields belfry inspection and a quarter-hour hold. Theft plus danger yields emergency manor entry and watch support, but no automatic publication. Authentication plus public witness enters the deposition and trustee response into the same-day council record. Any three combine warrant, hold, and record. All four divide the board and place Dorr’s obstruction beside the evidence. Once written, these outputs persist.

A refusal also travels. A denied warrant bears the rejected proof in Dorr’s hand. Renn can preserve the gallery and shadow the carriage without exceeding it. A lost cancellation demand may still win a hold, belfry inspection, or permission for the West Door families to withdraw. Covert records may fail formal authentication and still move Maelin or Corven. A confrontation may close the vault and open the chamber windows to the crowd.

Dorr did not build the rite. His fault is choosing controlled disclosure over the people who pay for delay. He can accept split custody, a timed public reading, a guarded search, or a warning pattern that preserves order without preserving silence. He rejects invented occult motives. Expose him, bargain with him, bypass him, or make him sign the refusal. A forum secured here matters to Edrin because it already holds records, witnesses, and custody; another private review does not.

**If skipped or reached late.** Dorr acts on reports that reach him. Without contrary evidence he orders containment, preserves the peal, and calls the rupture theft and vandalism. He cannot invent the archive or Tavia’s location. The other trustees keep their divisions. Every order, abstention, and limited inspection remains usable later. Once copies, witnesses, or a warning peal spread, even Dorr’s preferred hearing begins from public facts.

reference_links.context: Independent authentication of Olyra’s history can divide the trustees and make continued containment publicly costly.
Her empty chair, family interest, and museum seal force a public choice among curatorial office, Vale testimony, and institutional control.
A credible public hearing and custody plan can reach him; another sealed review cannot.
Her admission can establish theft and sabotage, while the chamber’s custody terms determine whether she will testify publicly.
Controls the agenda and procession seal; the quality, custody, danger, and public witness of the proof determine his available orders.
Appears to request an exact order; the chamber’s proof and written scope determine what the watch may do next.
Her documented chain can satisfy independent authentication and preserves any order that closes the public stair or removes her from duty.
Dorr’s dismissal of her and the survivor families makes their conditions, material evidence, and willingness to testify part of the hearing.
A named public custodian and authenticated House copy can force same-day entry while keeping the original dispute outside one institutional seal.
The draft seizure order targets its ledgers; any signed order, split caucus, or distributed packet becomes part of the public-pressure state.
Its doors, frames, records, and living witnesses provide independent proof that the chamber may hear, dismiss, or publicly answer.
Installation and inspection orders make the chamber’s narrow authority over the crown tower concrete without transferring technical control from its crew.

encounters.title: The West Infirmary
encounters.summary: A working hospice preserves Olyra’s defiance in doors, frames, cloth, and living terms no Vale or trustee may claim wholesale.
encounters.opening_view: “Not the glass,” Caldra Fen says, finishing a bandage. “The people who remember it.” Behind her, clear panes fill the shrine gaps above sleeping patients. The old fever doors preserve both commands: seal us in, cut us out. Survivor names cover one table, paired with questions for a saint who may answer in borrowed words. No family has signed away its testimony, relics, or grief.
encounters.content:
Caldra finishes a bandage before she discusses the record. She controls the fever doors and every approach to the occupied ward. Ilye Aven keeps the bed-frame tallies and will make rubbings without moving the frames. Tomar Ordel holds a family copy of Olyra’s final instructions and distrusts every Vale, Iria included. The Sorn line appears in the burial register; Tavia’s crime grants neither guilt nor authority to her relatives. Care continues while the city debates its dead.

The evidence remains in use: names cut into bed frames, burial cloth marked by Olyra’s hand, the council order nailed to one fever door, axe cuts opening the other from within, and histories kept by separate households. Empty shrine frames show where Alis removed the colored panes. Edrin’s recent measurements trace a maintenance route toward the winter garden, and his written question—would the families testify if the saint called them?—has Caldra’s answer beneath it: they will testify for Olyra; they will not be commanded by her image.

Commitment costs labor and trust. Caldra speaks if another healer covers the ward and the record stays outside trustee and Vale custody. Ilye brings rubbings and the tally key, never the frames. Tomar reads the family copy if Iria acknowledges the concealment without asking forgiveness in the same breath. Two other families will sign but will not enter the court. Meet those terms to gain authentication, public witnesses, and a West Door delegation. Pressure patients, take objects, or promise vindication from the Glass Saint, and particular witnesses withdraw. The history remains.

Tavia may seek refuge here. If trustee seizure threatens the House, she brings the cut leaf because her ancestor’s name appears on it. Caldra will not hide her from a lawful public charge or hand her into a closed museum transfer. She insists that confession, leaf, and family testimony be heard together. Show Tavia the chapel’s vocal cost or Alis’s warning and she turns toward cooperation. Condemn Edrin alone and she remains unmoved; she already knows the theft was unlawful and judged silence worse.

Late in the day, ordinary window glass begins repeating nearby prayers. The fragments attack no one and answer nothing; they show the rite gathering the city’s language. A completed agreement can send rubbings, testimony, a West Door delegation, or the maintenance route forward, but no patient or original frame leaves the ward. Without investigator agreements, Ilye still sends a rubbing to Nessa Quill and Tomar still tells the West Door families the question has reopened. This place moves on its own terms.

**If skipped or reached late.** Names on a page create no promise of testimony, custody, or a breath-giver from Caldra. West Door families follow commitments already made in the court; otherwise they remain at the hospice or withdraw independently. The doors, copies, empty frames, and maintenance measurements remain. If a bell command reaches the ward, resolve what it does to patients and staff before treating the hospice as uncomplicated support.

reference_links.context: Doors, frames, cloth, household memory, and living witnesses preserve evidence that neither relic nor archive can supply alone.
Her family knowledge and public acknowledgment can support the hospice witnesses, while her position must never substitute for their testimony or consent.
His measurements and questions test survivor testimony while revealing that the living families reject command by Olyra’s image.
Her family appears in the burial register; the hospice offers testimony and conditional refuge without granting her relatives’ authority.
Dismisses Caldra and survivor families as interested witnesses, making his treatment of independent testimony part of the case.
Runs the working hospice, controls patient access and testimony conditions, and can join refuge, confession, and family evidence under public protection.
Keeps the family petition copies named by the survivor index and can carry rubbings or signed testimony into distributed public custody.
Moved the first shrine’s colored panes to the manor, leaving the empty frames and warning trail that connect the hospice to the winter garden.
West Door copies and caucus commitments provide a route from family evidence to a public reading without moving patients or original frames.
The fever doors, working ward, survivor material, and separate family conditions remain the stable core beneath changing witness commitments.
Empty shrine frames and maintenance measurements reveal the undercroft passage while preserving the hospice’s independence from the manor.

encounters.title: The House of Petitions
encounters.summary: Petitioners expose the vow-bed’s contradictory language, judge Tavia’s confession, and decide how evidence will move through the city.
encounters.opening_view: A signed accusation reaches the rear copy window before its author reaches the front desk. Then another follows it. Shelves rise over cures, pardons, debts, births, disappearances, and refusals. Four caucuses argue across one table; copyists mark a warning-bell chart; petitioners press signed sheets into unfamiliar hands. Nessa Quill climbs onto a chair, not to quiet the room, but to keep every sheet moving while the doorway thickens.
encounters.content:
Four caucuses crowd Nessa Quill’s copy tables, each already moving a different packet. Open Hands want cures, pardons, debt relief, publication, and a stopped peal. Returned Names want answers for the missing and may accept Edrin’s rite. West Door Circle carries infirmary petitions and rejects both the obedience legend and compulsory command. Quiet Keepers fear that street action will close the office. Nessa keeps sheets moving between them; no one gets to make the room desire one ending.

The ledgers show that the vow-bed carries more than names. Its engravings repeat incompatible commands: obey lawful authority, protect children, punish betrayal, forgive debt, return the absent, make the city pure. Edrin tested mirrored silver against different petition sets; the figure’s language changed with the cards. Current copies can weight, contradict, or bound an answering form, but one afternoon cannot overwrite six decades of silver. The practical question is which sheets leave, in whose hands, and whether they can be heard before the bells.

Tavia is a culpable witness in motion. If she arrives unopposed, she brings the cut archive leaf, a bloodied cuff, and Edrin’s order to distribute the record before sunset. In **Defiance**, she admits the theft to Nessa, refuses trustee custody, and withholds the manor service route while she tests whether the investigators mean to bury the pages. Proof of the vocal cost plus custody outside private trustee control moves her to **Cooperation**. She then gives the full transfer statement, names chapel deliveries and the service route, and helps issue a warning, expecting arrest afterward. Under Renn’s public seal she testifies. A closed transfer ordered by Dorr ends her cooperation. Threatened with private seizure, destroyed evidence, or summary violence, she **Flees** to the infirmary with the leaf. Left unpersuaded and uncornered, she distributes copies and later goes to the manor to demand publication before the bell. Sabotage, Lio’s injury, and theft remain hers in every state.

Choose how the pages travel. A **certified reading** joins Senna’s or Caldra’s authentication to Nessa’s copy and creates a hearing Edrin may trust. A **distributed packet** places deposition, trustee minute, and witness statements with several keepers; suppression becomes difficult and rumor accelerates. A **public-custody pledge** names the future holders of records and recovered silver. A **warning assembly** sends petitioners toward belfry or manor, creating witnesses and crowd pressure. A **quiet escrow** protects records while yielding Dorr the first public account.

A seizure order begins a scene. The Quiet Keepers may divide from the other caucuses. Renn can reject private confiscation if the House names custodians and holds no stolen object. Investigators may negotiate split custody, pass copies through rear windows, read the order aloud, or defend the building. Violence wins paper and confirms Edrin’s belief that testimony receives force. If the House fractures, each caucus carries a piece elsewhere: Open Hands to the court, Returned Names toward the manor, West Door Circle to the infirmary, Quiet Keepers into private storage. Failure disperses the route; it never deletes it.

**If skipped or reached late.** Tavia gives Nessa the cut leaf and names the voice risk only if that knowledge has reached her. Open Hands begin public copies, Returned Names carry one packet toward the manor, West Door Circle sends one to the infirmary, and Quiet Keepers hide one off-site. Current petitions enter no apparatus by themselves; someone must carry and place them. A late group finds a constituency distributed across named destinations.

reference_links.context: Old and current petitions shape the public language attached to Olyra without granting any constituency sole ownership of her meaning.
His order puts publication before the bell, but Tavia and the petition caucuses may separate public record from his coercive plan.
Her defiance, cooperation, or flight determines the cut leaf, service route, confession, warning, and distribution available here.
May seek the ledgers or a closed transfer, but distributed copies and named caucuses can move the dispute beyond private containment.
A public watch seal can protect Tavia’s confession and custody without turning her over to a closed museum transfer.
Her certification can join a House copy to an authenticated source and create a hearing that survives private claims of forgery.
Her testimony or signed authentication can join survivor memory to the public packet without moving the ward into the House.
Coordinates caucuses, copies, custodians, readings, Tavia’s statement, and the destinations each packet takes if the room fractures.
Its four caucuses, copy ledgers, distributed custody, and incompatible aims define what public pressure can carry toward belfry and manor.
West Door Circle and family copies keep the petition record tied to living survivor authority rather than to the silver alone.
Tavia’s service sketch and any current petitions physically carried from the House shape access and the words available at the apparatus.

encounters.title: The Bell Chapel
encounters.summary: A rehearsal already speaking in borrowed voices reveals body, mouth, and reach; strip, cord, and deposition can answer the peal at different costs.
encounters.opening_view: The first word spoken in the chapel returns in a glass voice. No bell moves. Ropes narrow the nave; petition cards command from the floor; fresh wax binds a Vale ribbon into a mouth-shaped knot. A severed strand crosses the chalk road from museum to belfry to winter garden. Above, the practice clapper slips. Every rope answers.
encounters.content:
Edrin chose the chapel because its bell once called attendants to the west infirmary. The rehearsal has been left speaking. Four workings cross the nave: a mirrored frame over interchangeable petition cards; a mouth knot tied around a Vale hair ribbon; a relay board with six pin-shaped recesses; and a chalk route joining the Grand Belfry, East Gate, River Ward, and Vale Manor. Five intact pins appear on the plan. Cracked wax marks the spent museum trigger. The three Grand Belfry recesses read **witness**, **mouth**, and **crown**; the lesser towers read **relay**. Relay pins repeat the crown note. They cannot make the body or take a voice.

The rehearsal still answers. Exchange the petition cards and hand-sized glass attendants recite incompatible civic virtues. Put a hand inside the mouth knot and the nearest figure borrows the last sentence spoken in the room. Strike the relay board and the chapel bell answers without moving; one listener feels a sharp urge to obey the clearest imperative just heard. The figures fail to recognize Edrin, Olyra’s doors, or the same childhood memory twice. These tests separate language, voice, range, and instability. Let investigators stop after one proof, press for more certainty, or dismantle the workshop. Each additional test risks another line, pin, or spoken command.

The room punishes careless position. Waxed ropes tighten under crossed weight. A live pin snaps toward nearby bell metal. A cut tie drops the practice clapper through the nave. The wrong line sends a pulse that steals one complete sentence from the nearest speaker and gives it to the figures until the next bell note. Colored sleeves, tie-offs, and Edrin’s safe order reward a careful search. Tavia’s shorthand in the margin records the museum cut. Bell training, patient trials, or two workers approaching from opposite sides permit controlled dismantling. A rush still yields evidence, but may leave a pin live, damage one counterkey part, or preserve the investigators’ last imperative in the rehearsal.

The **counterkey** answers the rite in three pieces. The notched tuning strip identifies a live pin and lets a gloved hand lift it without carrying the vibration into the bell. The braided reversal cord changes a command knot into a confined or answering knot. The pitch table aligns those forms with the three long notes and the necessary lines of Olyra’s deposition. Strip alone: safe pin removal. Cord plus table: retuning. All three, Olyra’s text, and a willing breath-giver: bounded answering. A damaged set narrows the work; each surviving part keeps its listed use.

Every answer changes what the city will hear. Silence the witness bell and no body forms, but the procession loses its opening cadence. Lift the mouth pin after the first note and the glass body remains voiceless. Lift or mute the crown and the manor remains dangerous while the city escapes command. Retune the outer knot and confine the third note to everyone in the winter garden. Turn it outward into an answering form and a willing speaker lends one breath per answer, risking muteness until dawn. Remove the vow-bed and the speaking body collapses while the heartglass survives. Break the heartglass and every manifestation ends with Olyra’s last material relic.

Take any subset of tools, notes, and witnessed demonstrations. Record what survives, who saw each test, whether a sentence was stolen, and whether a practice pin remains live. Jori Kest can verify only what reaches him. Dorr can dismiss only what remains unsupported.

**If skipped or reached late.** Edrin does not return for the counterkey. Strip, cord, and table remain where Edrin left them until someone carries them out. The belfry can brake or damage a known bell without the set, but cannot safely lift live pins or retune with control. After the witness note, mouth and crown work still matters. After the mouth note, crown and warning work still matters. A late search yields the tools for the stages still ahead.

reference_links.context: Her deposition keys the counterkey, while rehearsal failures show that the glass figures cannot recover Olyra as a person.
His rehearsals, knot work, counterkey, and abandoned tools expose how the rite borrows language, voice, and reach.
Her deliveries and any proof of the vocal cost can separate her publication goal from Edrin’s mouth working.
Can dismiss unsupported claims, yet witnessed demonstrations and carried tools give later bell intervention an evidentiary basis.
Can verify and act on the strip, pitch table, and witnessed demonstration only after those materials or their proof reach his tower.
Her warning about a Vale voice gives the rehearsal’s mouth stage a documented family history and can turn Tavia toward cooperation.
The rope geometry, pane map, timing notes, and counterkey all describe how the manor chamber receives body, voice, and reach.
The ritual map and counterkey distinguish the three stage pins in the crown tower from relay pins that can repeat only the command.

encounters.title: The Grand Belfry
encounters.summary: Every rope is a public choice: the divided ringers can silence, confine, warn, or carry the rite, and bronze remembers what they do.
encounters.opening_view: Six ropes descend through the crew, three answer-pins humming among them. Jori Kest holds Dorr’s sealed order. Mela Fen strikes the locked wheel-loft door once from above. “First lift,” calls Rian Voss. “Full peal,” answers Karel Venn. The counterweight rises through their disagreement, hauling every command toward bronze. Nobody has released a rope; nobody has agreed what the city is about to hear.
encounters.content:
Name every hand on a rope before the first lift. Jori Kest directs the ringing room and will not gamble a ringer on an unexplained device. Rian Voss treats Dorr’s sealed order as the crew’s only shield. Mela Fen found Karel Venn in the wheel loft and has locked herself on the crown deck with the tuning ledger. Pavo Tern and Lis Aven hold tie-offs and carry messages; either may run when fear outruns discipline. Karel, one of the Returned Names, is trying to preserve the full peal because rumor convinced him delay would bury the record again. Edrin never sent him.

The crew is split across the tower: ropes and brakes below; live pins and moving counterweights in the loft; Mela, the ledger, and the bell mouths above. Once a bell moves, its rope lane can lift, drag, or strike anyone who crosses it. A loose counterweight can take the stairs. Bare metal against a humming pin carries its imperative into the next bell. Stop machinery, secure tie-offs, and control the crew before treating the tower as a puzzle.

The three live pins remain **witness**, **mouth**, and **crown**. The first raises the reflected body at Vale Manor; the second opens the nearest Vale as speaker; the crown launches the command to any connected relay. East Gate and River Ward can repeat only that third note. Removing the crown protects the city while leaving body and voice danger at the manor; removing all three stops the rite here, though Dorr can move ceremonial music to the lesser towers.

Put the case on the crew floor. The chapel strip identifies the linked pins; the pitch table and Mela’s ledger match stages to bells; Tavia can prove sabotage. A warrant or signed hold gives legal protection, while named petitioners or infirmary witnesses give public protection. One technical proof plus either form of cover is enough for controlled work. Without it, Rian calls the watch, a junior may run, and Dorr can call the intervention a second attack.

Choose what the bells will be allowed to do. **Strip all stage pins:** stop all three bells, secure the loft, and use the strip; every stage fails, the full peal is lost, and the crew is publicly implicated. **Lift the crown:** one controlled ascent prevents city-wide command while leaving body and voice danger at the manor. **Mute or bind one bell:** fast without the counterkey, dangerous under motion, and visible as sabotage; that stage remains silent until repaired. **Retune the sequence:** reversal cord, pitch table, Mela’s ledger, Kest or equivalent skill, and two cooperative ringers confine the crown note to the winter garden while preserving the first two. **Sound the warning:** two ringers and an intact warning bell draw watch, petitioners, and witnesses toward the manor; concealment ends, panic may begin. **Preserve the peal:** an informed choice for bounded answering or accepted risk.

A sounded note cannot be unsounded; every later note remains contestable. Before the witness note, every operation stands. After it, mouth, crown, retuning, and warning remain. After the mouth note, the Vale voice is already gone, but crown removal still protects the city and retuning still confines the command. Once the crown starts, braking the bell, breaking the pin, or severing the rope may reduce the relays; no action recalls a sounded command.
