encounters.title: Vale Manor
encounters.summary: At the winter garden, every copied page, opened door, altered bell, willing witness, and surviving pane determines what Edrin can still make speak.
encounters.opening_view: “You came before the bells,” Edrin Vale says. He stands inside the winter garden’s rope circle with the stolen silver beneath the suspended heartglass and an open dossier at his feet. Old shrine panes cast faces across the servants, the doors, and the witnesses gathering beyond the wall. One hand rests on the inner knot. Under the floor, the bell trunk gives a low tremor, and every pane returns a different face.
encounters.content:
Before Edrin speaks, read the city already gathered at the glass. Record the surviving stage and relay pins, any warning pattern, the procession’s position, the holders of authenticated copies, Captain Renn’s exact authority, witnesses and petitioners in motion, Tavia’s state, and whether Iria accompanies the investigators. A cut rope, public copy, signed denial, dispersed crowd, or lifted pin stays changed when the scene moves.

**Six ways through the doors.** A recovery or emergency-entry warrant brings Renn and four officers through the carriage gate. Its written scope protects servants, seals objects, and restrains named suspects; it also defines the overreach Dorr may later allege. Iria may claim the east door. Steward **Leva Orm** admits her and companions who accept a household inventory, while Iria’s presence creates a second possible Vale speaker. Tavia knows the laundry court and silver-pantry route to the garden side passage and vow-bed braces; covert speed costs public legitimacy unless someone outside knows the purpose. Infirmary measurements reveal a maintenance passage beneath the shrine frames, opening beside the bell trunk and four foundation anchors. A warning peal or petitioner march crosses the west lawn in public; Edrin opens the garden doors so the record cannot vanish, and the crowd brings crush, custody, and command risk. Direct force through doors, roof, or panes remains possible. It alarms the household and turns controlled glass and rope into falling hazards.

**The household at the glass.** Edrin begins on the speaker mark, dossier open, heartglass above the vow-bed, one hand on the mouth line. He takes no hostages and orders no servant to fight. Leva waits in the front hall with keys, servant roll, and a blank inventory. She wants the concealment ended and the coercive rite stopped. A lawful order, Iria’s acknowledgment, or proof of involuntary voice loss moves her into evacuation and active inventory. Indiscriminate violence makes her bar doors and protect people. Garden keeper and glazier **Peren Holt** waits beside the pane latches in the undercroft. Edrin promised a public display, not command. Show Peren a live mouth effect or Tavia’s account and he releases shutters, unseats panes, or guides investigators through the maintenance passage. Without proof he protects the old glass. Six servants remain in the detached kitchen court as witnesses and people to evacuate, never reserve combatants.

**Five joined things give the saint a body.** The **pane crown** mounts eight shrine panes in hinged iron frames. Open panes admit procession light and public reflections; shutters and released frames weaken the body and narrow what it can mirror. The **vow-bed table** holds the engraved silver and any current petitions placed during play. Remove, cover, or replace those words to change the available language; wrenching the bed free after manifestation throws sharp reflected phrases through the room. The **heartglass cradle** suspends Olyra’s relic over the silver. Lower and seal it to end a formed body. Break it to end every stage and Olyra’s last material link. The **inner mouth knot** marks the speaker circle. When the mouth note completes, the nearest living Vale inside the outer pane circle loses their natural voice. Edrin begins nearest. Iria becomes the target only by entering or remaining after he is moved beyond the circle. The mouth stage fails without either a Vale inside or a hand closing the inner line. The **bell trunk** carries witness, mouth, and crown vibrations under the floor. Tie off an unsounded branch from the undercroft; a sounded branch is history.

**Edrin listens only for a hearing that already exists.** Edrin begins in **Declaration**. He admits theft and sabotage, displays the dossier, and says the museum forfeited the right to choose its own hearing. One public anchor—a same-day council entry, certified records outside Vale and museum custody, named witnesses present or audibly assembling, a warning peal, or petitioners reading the deposition—moves him to **Pause** before the witness note. He hears exact terms and allows inspection; Dorr’s sealed promise still means nothing. Two independent anchors plus named custody for heartglass, vow-bed, and dossier move him to **Witnessed Terms**. He opens the outer knot, leaves the speaker mark, and negotiates surrender, public reading, or bounded answering. Tavia’s public rejection of the vocal cost, Iria’s acknowledgment, and Jori’s certification alter his posture but do not replace custody. Private seizure, destroyed copies, or an unannounced assault moves him to **Hardened Assembly**. He closes doors and advances the next available trigger, without taking hostages or attacking a surrendered witness. New public facts can move him back to Pause even after the body forms.

Move Edrin only when pages, witnesses, custody, or altered glass make his next position untenable. Ask what has become public, who holds each object, and which promise survives tomorrow’s change of office or family mind.

**The three notes borrow body, voice, and reach in order.** Before the **witness note**, inventory, negotiation, sealed custody, zone-by-zone dismantling, and reversal all remain possible. An intact witness pin casts light from the panes across the vow-bed and raises a translucent human outline. It recites incompatible petition fragments and civic virtues. It answers no question and recognizes no relic. The body persists while heartglass, silver, and four pane frames remain joined. Remove the heartglass, separate the bed, or release enough frames to collapse it.

An intact **mouth note** completed while Edrin closes the knot takes the nearest living Vale’s natural voice. The body speaks in that timbre without the speaker’s will or memory. Move a Vale before completion to change the target; carrying the speaker away afterward does not restore the voice. Cut or reverse the knot before completion to prevent involuntary transfer. With all three counterkey parts, Olyra’s deposition, a willing breath-giver, and witnessed consent, tie the reversal cord outward. The answering form borrows breath until dawn, remains inside the garden, and answers at most three questions from records and petitions physically present. It reveals no unknown fact, hidden culprit, or proof that it is Olyra. Uncertainty comes as contradiction, silence, or an irrelevant petition.

An intact **crown note** takes its range from the belfry record. No crown pin, no launched command. A retuned crown confines it to the winter garden. One relay reaches its connected wards; two reach the procession route. Derive its language from three streams recorded before arrival: the vow-bed’s old engravings, current petitions physically added, and the phrase most publicly repeated by Edrin, petitioners, trustees, or investigators. A phrase supported by two streams governs. If all three conflict, the intact vow-bed’s most repeated civic formula governs unless deliberately covered or altered. Use a short command whose ordinary readings produce aid and danger. The body speaks only from the recorded streams; it cannot settle Olyra’s meaning.

**Every command opens one door and breaks another.** “Open the doors” frees sealed wards and records while opening prisons, sickrooms, homes, and dangerous works. “Speak the names” restores suppressed victims and exposes protected identities, accusations, and private grief. “Forgive the debts” breaks predatory claims and also wages, care obligations, restitution, and common stores. “Return them” sends people after family, fugitives, exiles, and the dead. “Protect the children” produces shelter, abduction, family conflict, and violent paternalism. “Obey the wounded” centers neglected testimony and grants contradictory demands coercive force. Derive any new command from established language and name at least one aid and one danger before it sounds.

**What survives decides the ending.** **Witnessed surrender** preserves the apparatus under split custody and sends Edrin to prosecution without manifestation. **Dismantling before the witness note** prevents supernatural evidence while leaving the documentary dispute. **Bounded answering** yields up to three composite replies, temporary muteness, and a contested public source. **Witness-only manifestation** creates observers without stolen voice or command. **Voice taken, crown stopped** leaves one Vale mute unless restored before dawn and protects the city. A **confined command** reaches garden and west lawn; a **partial relay** divides East Gate from River Ward; a **full awakening** compels the procession until dawn. **Heartglass destruction** ends the body and may leave a taken voice unrestored. **Violent failure** follows the damaged zone: falling panes, trapped bodies, broken silver, or one surviving relay.

Write the ending on separate lines: body formed; voice taken; command and range; condition and custodian of heartglass, vow-bed, panes, counterkey, and dossier; witnesses to each stage; injuries, detentions, and commitments.

**Before dawn, the stolen voice may choose return.** An involuntary transfer outlives the figure. The original speaker may consent in writing to a reversed mouth working before dawn. It needs intact heartglass, reversal cord, mouth-pitch cue, and one independent witness. Seal the heartglass over an empty or covered vow-bed, tie the inner line outward, and let the speaker choose whether to reclaim the voice. Success returns it and leaves the heartglass acoustically inert. Destroyed heartglass, lost cord, dawn, or refusal makes the muteness lasting. Edrin’s surrender restores nothing by itself.

**After the bells, the city keeps five reckonings.** **Custody:** name a holder and access rule for every surviving object; split custody may include watch, infirmary, House, museum, or a new trust. **Publication:** distinguish council entry, witnessed reading, distributed dispute, and resealed originals; spoken or copied knowledge persists. **Prosecution:** Edrin answers for conspiracy, receiving stolen civic property, and attempted compulsion; Tavia for sabotage, Lio’s injury, theft, and evidence removal, with cooperation and prevented harm as mitigation; Dorr and participating trustees for concealment and obstruction; Iria politically and professionally for what she knew, withheld, certified, or disclosed. **Surviving compulsion:** mark affected rooms or wards, concrete emergencies, and the institutions responding before dawn. **Olyra’s memory:** record what is authenticated, disputed, fractured, memorialized, exhibited, or managed into another silence.

End when immediate coercion and physical danger are resolved. Close with named custody, testimony, accusations, and one visible public consequence. The city may finally know that Olyra opened the west doors without agreeing what her defiance asks of it now.
